context: Direct ProofWiki Definition 1. Countable-union and relative-complement conditions are not interchangeable with arbitrary-union topological axioms; X may be empty. Do not equate sigma-algebra with topology.
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki Definition 1. Countable-union and relative-complement conditions are not interchangeable with arbitrary-union topological axioms; X may be empty. Do not equate sigma-algebra with topology.
text: For a set X, a sigma-algebra Σ on X is a family Σ⊆P(X) such that X∈Σ; if A∈Σ then X\A∈Σ; and for every countable sequence (A_n) with each A_n∈Σ, the union ⋃_{n≥1}A_n belongs to Σ.

context: Direct ProofWiki Definition 2. Values may be +infinity; zero on the empty set and countable additivity for pairwise disjoint measurable sets are explicit. Do not infer probability normalization μ(X)=1 or finite total mass.
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki Definition 2. Values may be +infinity; zero on the empty set and countable additivity for pairwise disjoint measurable sets are explicit. Do not infer probability normalization μ(X)=1 or finite total mass.
text: Let Σ be a sigma-algebra on a set X. A (nonnegative) measure is a function μ:Σ→[0,+∞] such that μ(∅)=0 and μ(⋃_{n=1}^∞ E_n)=∑_{n=1}^∞ μ(E_n) whenever (E_n) is a sequence of pairwise disjoint sets in Σ.
